Mozart's birthplace combines urban vibrancy with close proximity to nature, creating a city atmosphere where tradition, culture and landscape come together with ease.</p><p textalign="null"><strong>The best of Salzburg and SalzburgerLand:</strong></p><ul><li><p textalign="null">All about the <a href="/en-gb/cities-and-places/salzburg/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">city of Salzburg</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null">All about <a href="/en-gb/provinces/salzburgerland/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">SalzburgerLand</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null"><a href="/en-gb/highlights/salzburgerland-sights/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Top sights in SalzburgerLand</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null"><a href="/en-gb/profiles/wolfgang-amadeus-mozart/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null"><a href="/en-gb/locations/moenchsberg/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">A walk on the Mönchsberg</a></p></li></ul></div><!-- --><div class="flex items-center gap-4 rounded-xl border border-white/20 p-4 bg-red-50"><div class="bg-red-800 self-start rounded-full p-1.5"><span aria-hidden="true" class="iconify i-oew:award-outline block size-5 text-white" dynamic="" style=""></span></div><!--[--><div class="prose" data-v-2c23d0bf=""><p textalign="null">Salzburg's Old Town was designated a <a class="external-link inline align-baseline" href="https://www.unesco.at/en/culture/world-heritage/world-heritage-sites-in-austria" rel="noopener" target="_blank">UNESCO World Heritage Site</a> in 1996. Churches, palaces and parks shape the cityscape, lending the 1st district its imperial character. A rich musical tradition, extensive collections, classic coffee houses and historic purveyors to the court complete the cultural experience. Vienna's Old Town remains a living testament to Habsburg architecture, culture and history.</p><p textalign="null"><strong>The best of Vienna:</strong></p><ul><li><p textalign="null">All about <a href="/en-gb/cities-and-places/vienna/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Vienna</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null"><a href="/en-gb/inspiration/coffeehouse-culture/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Viennese coffee house culture</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null"><a href="/en-gb/locations/st-stephens-cathedral/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">St Stephen's Cathedral</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null"><a href="/en-gb/profiles/vienna-philharmonic/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">The Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra</a></p></li></ul></div><!-- --><div class="flex items-center gap-4 rounded-xl border border-white/20 p-4 bg-red-50"><div class="bg-red-800 self-start rounded-full p-1.5"><span aria-hidden="true" class="iconify i-oew:award-outline block size-5 text-white" dynamic="" style=""></span></div><!--[--><div class="prose" data-v-2c23d0bf=""><p textalign="null"><span style="color: ">Vienna's historic centre was declared a </span><span style="color: "><a class="external-link inline align-baseline" href="https://www.unesco.at/en/culture/world-heritage/world-heritage-sites-in-austria" rel="noopener" target="_blank">UNESCO World Heritage Site</a></span><span style="color: "> in 2001. Between the Schlossberg hill and the River Mur, Gothic churches, Renaissance courtyards and Baroque town houses trace the city’s development, complemented by the Baroque residence of the Eggenberg family. Since the Middle Ages, Graz has been a crossroads between the Balkans, the Alps and the Mediterranean, and under the Habsburgs it served as the residence of Emperor Frederick III. Eggenberg Palace, begun in 1625, is surrounded by extensive grounds that were redesigned as a landscape garden in the 19th century.</p><p textalign="null"><strong>The best of Graz and Styria:</strong></p><ul><li><p textalign="null">All about <a href="/en-gb/cities-and-places/graz/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Graz</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null">All about <a href="/en-gb/provinces/styria/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Styria</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null"><a class="external-link inline align-baseline" href="https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/palace-and-gardens-schloss-eggenberg" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Eggenberg Palace</a></p></li></ul></div><!-- --><div class="flex items-center gap-4 rounded-xl border border-white/20 p-4 bg-red-50"><div class="bg-red-800 self-start rounded-full p-1.5"><span aria-hidden="true" class="iconify i-oew:award-outline block size-5 text-white" dynamic="" style=""></span></div><!--[--><div class="prose" data-v-2c23d0bf=""><p textalign="null">Graz's historic centre was designated a <a class="external-link inline align-baseline" href="https://www.unesco.at/en/culture/world-heritage/world-heritage-sites-in-austria" rel="noopener" target="_blank">UNESCO World Heritage Site</a> in 1999, with Eggenberg Palace added in 2010. Its historic townscape combines elegant spa architecture, buildings from the imperial era and the open landscapes of the Vienna Woods. The Kurpark remains the green heart of this long-standing spa tradition. Baden was also a place of new ideas. The remains, dating from the Neolithic to the Iron Age, lie in wetlands and along lake shores, offering valuable insight into early societies.</p><p textalign="null">Austria is home to five such sites, including locations on Lake Attersee, Lake Mondsee and Lake Keutschach. Tools and materials such as copper and iron document trade networks, technical innovation and cultural exchange. The oldest settlement in Lake Keutschach dates back to the 4th millennium BC. The Mondsee site reveals trading links with Bavaria and northern Italy, while the settlements on Lake Attersee were established between 1690 and 1260 BC.</p><p textalign="null"><strong>The best of the Alps and Austria's lakes:</strong></p><ul><li><p textalign="null"><a href="/en-gb/inspiration/alps/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">The Alps</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null"><a href="/en-gb/locations/lake-attersee/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Lake Attersee</a></p></li><li><p textalign="null"><a href="/en-gb/locations/mondsee/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Lake Mondsee</a></p></li></ul></div><!-- --><div class="flex items-center gap-4 rounded-xl border border-white/20 p-4 bg-red-50"><div class="bg-red-800 self-start rounded-full p-1.5"><span aria-hidden="true" class="iconify i-oew:award-outline block size-5 text-white" dynamic="" style=""></span></div><!--[--><div class="prose" data-v-2c23d0bf=""><p textalign="null">The prehistoric pile dwellings were designated a <a class="external-link inline align-baseline" href="https://www.unesco.at/en/culture/world-heritage/world-heritage-sites-in-austria" rel="noopener" target="_blank">UNESCO World Heritage Site</a> in 2011.
